title: User-Defined SQL Functions
description: Write lightweight, inlinable user-defined functions in plain SQL with parameter binding and volatility markers.

data.text: PostgreSQL allows defining functions written in pure SQL (`LANGUAGE sql`). SQL functions can be **inlined** by the query planner, meaning the optimizer inserts the function query directly into the caller's query plan with zero function-call overhead!

rows: Always returns same result for same inputs; can be pre-computed in index expressions.
Result stays constant within a single query execution; scans can cache results.
Result can change at any moment; optimizer cannot cache calls.

data.title: Pure SQL Function with Inlining Capability

data.text: Using a SQL Function Inside an Index

Because a `LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE` function can be inlined and is guaranteed to return the same result for the same inputs, it can be used in an index expression. That lets you index computed values without repeating the formula everywhere it is queried.

data.title: Indexing a value computed by a function
data.content: The function must be `IMMUTABLE` for the index to be valid; a `STABLE` function is rejected by `CREATE INDEX`.

data.title: Volatility has to be honest
data.text: If you mark a function `IMMUTABLE` when it actually depends on session state, time zones, or table contents, PostgreSQL may fold it to a constant or store stale values in an index. Use `IMMUTABLE` only for pure computations, `STABLE` for functions that read data or the transaction timestamp, and `VOLATILE` for anything with side effects or randomness.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Plain SQL functions can be inlined by the optimizer for maximum speed.
Only `IMMUTABLE` functions can be used in Expression Indexes.
